question: A scientist has three radiations: A, B and C. Radiation A is used for sterilisation, radiation B is used for medical diagnosis, and radiation C is used in radar. Identify A, B and C. Arrange them in increasing order of wavelength and justify your answer.

options.A:
$A=$ ultraviolet rays; $B=$ X-rays; $C=$ microwaves.
Increasing order of wavelength: X-rays, ultraviolet rays, microwaves $(B,A,C)$.
X-rays have shorter wavelength than ultraviolet rays, and microwaves have the greatest wavelength among the three.
options.B:
$A=$ gamma rays; $B=$ ultraviolet rays; $C=$ radio waves.
Increasing order of wavelength: gamma rays, ultraviolet rays, radio waves $(A,B,C)$.
Sterilisation, medical diagnosis and radar correspond respectively to these radiations.
options.C:
$A=$ infrared rays; $B=$ X-rays; $C=$ ultraviolet rays.
Increasing order of wavelength: X-rays, ultraviolet rays, infrared rays $(B,C,A)$.
Infrared rays are used for sterilisation and ultraviolet rays are used in radar.
options.D:
$A=$ ultraviolet rays; $B=$ X-rays; $C=$ microwaves.
Increasing order of wavelength: microwaves, ultraviolet rays, X-rays $(C,A,B)$.
Microwaves have the shortest wavelength because they are used in radar.
